title: Meaning Beyond the Author
text:
Literary critics have long debated whether a text's meaning resides in the author's intentions or in the reader's interpretation. Formalists, by contrast, argued that a work should be analysed on its own terms, independent of the writer's biography. Reader-response theorists went further, contending that the text remains incomplete until a reader activates it. This tension remains productive, since each position exposes blind spots in the others.

Deconstruction, associated with Jacques Derrida, challenged the assumption that language can fix a single, stable meaning. Critics working in this vein often expose contradictions that the text itself tries to suppress. Such readings are sometimes dismissed as mere wordplay, yet their proponents maintain that they reveal how assumptions about meaning are constructed.

questions.text: According to the passage, what did Formalists argue?
options: That texts should be read through the author's biography.
That a work should be analysed on its own terms, independent of biography.
That meaning is completed only by the reader.
That language always has one fixed meaning.

questions.text: What do deconstructive critics often expose, according to the passage?
options: Contradictions the text tries to suppress.
Grammatical errors in the author's work.
Historical facts missing from the text.

questions.text: Why might deconstructive readings be dismissed as mere wordplay?
options: Because they treat language as too unstable to yield a fixed interpretation, which some critics find unrigorous.
Because they ignore the reader entirely.
Because they analyse only the author's biography.
Because they accept a single fixed meaning for every text.

questions.text: The passage suggests that the tension between critical positions is
options: a sign that literary criticism has failed.
valuable, because each view reveals limitations in the others.

paragraph_translations: Los críticos literarios han debatido durante mucho tiempo si el significado de un texto reside en las intenciones del autor o en la interpretación del lector. Los formalistas, en cambio, sostenían que una obra debe analizarse en sus propios términos, independientemente de la biografía del escritor. Los teóricos de la recepción fueron más lejos, afirmando que el texto permanece incompleto hasta que un lector lo activa. Esta tensión sigue siendo fructífera, ya que cada postura expone los puntos ciegos de las demás.

La deconstrucción, asociada a Jacques Derrida, cuestionó la suposición de que el lenguaje puede fijar un único significado estable. Los críticos que trabajan en esta línea suelen exponer contradicciones que el propio texto intenta reprimir. Estas lecturas a veces se descartan como un simple juego de palabras, pero sus partidarios sostienen que revelan cómo se construyen las suposiciones sobre el significado.
